A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WyckoffDiff. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching v2 Appendices D–E to v3 Appendices F–G.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 report original WBM generation experiments, energy analyses and DFT calculations for selected generated materials. Appendices C and E provide further results.

after.justification: The original generation and materials-discovery results remain. Appendices D–E additionally report compositional-validity measurements and Carbon24 experiments.

M1.justification: The representation, WyckoffGNN architecture, training loss and diffusion procedure are retained. Algorithm 1 equivalently reindexes sampling steps. The earlier marginal architecture in v3 Appendix G.3 already appeared in v2 Appendix E.3; Carbon24 uses a different configuration of the same method.

E1.justification: v3 retains WBM and the materials-discovery study and adds Carbon24 training and evaluation in Appendix E. This introduces a distinct single-element carbon domain where novel protostructures necessarily require novel prototypes, substantially extending the represented evaluation conditions.

E2.justification: CDVAE, DiffCSP++ and SymmCD remain the evaluated baselines. The Carbon24 and compositional-validity comparisons use this same set. The expanded WyCryst discussion does not introduce an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The existing WBM splits, training budget and 10,000-sample evaluation remain. v3 adds Carbon24-specific settings: 4,000 training epochs, P=24, and evaluation using 1,000 generated and 1,000 novel protostructures. Appendix D also adds SMACT compositional validity as an evaluation metric.

E4.justification: Section 4.1 adds a diagnostic comparison of CDVAE and WBM space-group frequencies, and Appendix D adds a compositional-validity analysis. The prior-distribution and training-duration comparisons, energy histograms and materials-discovery case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report WBM means and standard deviations from three differently seeded models. The additional results continue the existing plus/minus reporting practice; no new run-count specification, significance test, confidence interval or uncertainty-estimation procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises marginal-model results: FWD changes from 0.58±0.03 to 0.55±0.05 at 1,000 epochs and from 1.90±0.49 to 1.65±0.07 at 100 epochs, alongside novelty and uniqueness updates. Table 2 changes marginal prototype counts from 1175±80 to 733±11 and zeros counts from 926±42 to 1175±80; marginal now falls below SymmCD's 780±49. v3 also adds Carbon24 Tables 4–5, compositional-validity scores and space-group frequencies. The energy plots and DFT material energies are retained.

T1.justification: The formal representation, diffusion mathematics and scheduler remain substantively unchanged. Equation 5 explicitly expresses the same transition as a categorical distribution, and Algorithm 1 uses equivalent timestep indexing. No new theorem, proof or substantive derivation appears.

C1.justification: The central claims about symmetry-preserving generation, the neural architecture, fast sampling, FWD and materials discovery retain their scope. v3 adds the stability demonstration to the abstract, but this contribution was already claimed in v2's introduction and Section 5.

C2.justification: v3 links CDVAE's high FWD to symmetry mismatch and explicitly interprets reduced novelty with longer training as memorization. New passages discuss complete-graph scalability limits, qualify SMACT validity for real materials, and attribute Carbon24's low novelty to its single-element setting. Existing energy and discovery interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v3 documents Carbon24's training-set source and configuration, identifies SMACT for the added validity check, and expands the availability statement from code to data and code. Section 3.4 changes P=55 to P=54, resolving its discrepancy with Table 3, which already specified 54 in v2. Existing hardware, architecture and DFT details remain.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 adds a direct representation and sampling comparison with SymmCD and a dedicated discussion distinguishing WyCryst's representation and ternary-material scope. Davies et al. (SMACT) and Pickard (Carbon24) are newly cited. WyCryst was already cited, and SymmCD's publication update refers to the same work.

P1.justification: The main section order and most prose remain. v3 makes localized explanatory additions, expands the abstract, adds departmental affiliations, CRediT contributions and an impact statement, and inserts appendix sections. The previous stability and discovery appendices are retained under new letters.

P2.justification: v3 comprehensively adopts ICML typesetting, changing typography, heading and caption styles, running headers, citation coloring and page composition. Existing tables and figures are repositioned, including placing Table 2 and Figure 2 beside each other. Carbon24 Tables 4–5 are added; v2's materials table remains as Table 6.

improvement.justification: Carbon24 provides a useful test beyond WBM that exposes low novelty and a different novel-only FWD ranking, while compositional-validity testing and explicit scalability and applicability limits improve empirical scrutiny and interpretation. These are modest gains around a retained method and discovery study. They are tempered by Section 4.2's broad superiority wording, which is not qualified to reflect the revised marginal prototype count falling below SymmCD.
